L8·N4548unmasked layer
Not a clean token detector — it fires weakly on ordinary function words/punctuation (" at", " to", " you", "'t", newline) inside technical/product or gaming-forum prose (ECU tuning, coil springs, paylines, timestamps), and is strongly suppressed on tokens in social-issue/historical narrative text (women's rights, anti-alcohol activism, dates like 1877), so it behaves as a topical context signal rather than a lexical one.

L8·N6791unmasked layer
This neuron fires on the completing token of a highly predictable multi-token noun — typically the last word/sub-word of a food or menu item in a list (Sal-"ads", Sh-"rimp" & Grits, meatball "sandwich") or of a fixed collocation/proper name (Saturday "morning", Schl-"itz"); its strongest negative responses come from the same kind of item-final food/name tokens (Escal-"ade", "wings", "vodka", fr-"ats").

L8·N9237unmasked layer
Primarily a suppression neuron: it goes strongly negative on tokens marking requests for/mentions of explanation or causation ("Why" + "?", "the reasons why", "logic behind"), while its weak positive side fires on mid-word subword continuations of proper names and similar word-internal fragments ("Hock|ney", "Mosser|i", "Muktin|ath", "lik|eli|est").
